stem: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled deck of 52 playing cards. What is the probability that the card drawn is either a King or a Heart?

per_option_rationale.rationale: P(King or Heart) = P(King) + P(Heart) - P(King of Hearts) = 4/52 + 13/52 - 1/52 = 16/52 = 4/13.
Adding P(King) + P(Heart) = 4/52 + 13/52 = 17/52 without subtracting the overlap (King of Hearts), treating the events as if they share no element.
Applying the inclusion-exclusion formula but mis-simplifying 16/52 without converting to lowest terms, leaving the answer as 16/52 instead of 4/13.
Using only the Heart count alone: 13/52 = 1/4, ignoring the King events entirely.

explanation: The addition theorem states P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B) for any two events. Here A = King (4 cards), B = Heart (13 cards), and A and B = King of Hearts (1 card). So P = (4 + 13 - 1)/52 = 16/52 = 4/13.

explanation_sections.punchline: The overlap (King of Hearts) is counted in both King and Heart groups, so it must be subtracted once.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: addition theorem for non-mutually-exclusive events. Map each given: n(King)=4, n(Heart)=13, n(King and Heart)=1, total=52. Apply P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B) = (4+13-1)/52 = 16/52 = 4/13.
explanation_sections.lesson: Whenever two events can occur simultaneously, always subtract their intersection to avoid double-counting.
explanation_sections.timing: 45 seconds. Eliminate 1/4 first (only counts Hearts). The trap is forgetting to subtract the King of Hearts.
